This ADR fixes the viewport stack as root stretch disabled with every scale chosen by script (a world `SubViewport` in a `SubViewportContainer`, then `CanvasLayer`s for hold, HUD, menus and debug), derives all geometry in one pure `RenderLayout` function written only by a single pipeline root, implements zoom as a change of logical size, defaults to render pass A with pass B behind one build flag, pins Forward+ and the Vulkan driver on Windows provisionally and explicitly (reversible at the lighting spike), writes the camera as a direct `canvas_transform` in `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`, and carries the single draw-call and timing budget table.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable, mono build installed), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Rendering (2D), with Core (frame hook) and UI (layer scaling) edges |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | HIGH. 4.6 made glow run before tonemapping and (per the reference) made D3D12 the Windows default; 4.7 removed the antialiasing feather from `CanvasItem` lines, added HDR output, and changed the stretch defaults for new projects. The pinned reference has no content on `SubViewport` 2D sizing, `size_2d_override`, `size_2d_override_stretch`, `use_hdr_2d`, `Light2D` under those, or `frame_pre_draw`. |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 Rendering and Project rows; 4.5 to 4.6 Rendering rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `modules/rendering.md`. `modules/ui.md` and `current-best-practices.md` were not read for this ADR (UI scaling is decided here from probes; dual focus is ADR-0030's). |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None required by the decision. Relevant post-cutoff facts it accounts for: D3D12 as the Windows default (4.6), glow before tonemapping (4.6), line drawing without a feather (4.7), HDR output flag (4.7; kept off), new-project stretch defaults `canvas_items` / `expand` (4.7; not relied on), Shader Baker (4.5; export option). |
27	| **Probed 2026-10-28 (installed 4.7.2, headless, members and arithmetic only)** | See the list below the table. |
28	| **Verification Required** | (1) Pipeline spike step 11: the wiring of § 2 draws the world at exactly `(k_z, k_z)` and the HUD at exactly `(H, H)` at every window in PR-1's table, read back by the chain in § 5.4, on a dev build and a release export; the first frame after each resize shows no fractional transform; the letterbox residual of an awkward window (1365x768) is black. (2) Spike step 11/12: `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` of the frame and a `canvas_transform` written in it is the one drawn that frame (NOT probed: the signal never fires under `--headless`); fallback and trigger in § 6. (3) Lighting spike steps 1, 2 and 9: printed driver and method, pass A vs pass B on the 16.6 ms criteria, Compatibility parity; these gate § 1 and § 4. (4) Lighting spike steps 7 and 8: whether `SubViewport.use_hdr_2d` (world only, root stays SDR) gives the ambient floor and glow the Lighting GDD needs, and whether `use_debanding` stays off (flat palette fills read back bit-exact). (5) Whether the project settings `snap_2d_*` and the default texture filter reach the world `SubViewport` (probed: the `SubViewport` members default to `false` and `1` independently of the project values, so the pipeline sets them explicitly regardless). (6) Container behaviour: that a `SubViewportContainer` with `stretch = false` and an integer `scale` draws its viewport texture with the container's `texture_filter` (NEAREST), without mipmaps and without a one-pixel bleed at the edge, under both passes. (7) Windows display scaling at 125 % and 150 % with `allow_hidpi` true (default, probed): the window pixel size the pipeline reads is physical pixels. (8) Release-export draw-call counts per viewport (`Viewport.get_render_info`) and the P99 table of § 7 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. |
29	
30	**Probed 2026-10-28 on the installed 4.7.2 editor (headless; transforms, sizes, members and defaults only):**
31	- **Built-in defaults.** `display/window/stretch/mode = disabled`, `aspect = keep`, `scale_mode = fractional` (so a project that writes none of them runs at 1152x648 unscaled, not at the `canvas_items` / `expand` the 4.7 migration row describes for new projects, which is an editor project-template behaviour); `display/window/size/viewport_width/height = 1152 / 648`; `window_width_override` and `window_height_override` = 0; `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = vulkan` (the engine built-in; this conflicts with the reference's "D3D12 is the Windows default", see Open Question OQ-C); `rendering/renderer/rendering_method = forward_plus`; `rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter = 1` (linear); `rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel = false`; `rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color = (0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1)`; `rendering/viewport/hdr_2d = false`; `rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_debanding = false`; `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`; `display/window/vsync/vsync_mode = 1` (enabled); `application/run/low_processor_mode = false`; `display/window/dpi/allow_hidpi = true`; `gui/common/snap_controls_to_pixels = true`.

34	- **`SubViewportContainer` defaults.** `stretch` false; `stretch_shrink` 1; `mouse_target` false; `texture_filter` 0 (`PARENT_NODE`; `CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` is 1); `material` null. `CanvasLayer.layer` 1, `scale` (1,1), `transform` identity. `Camera2D.zoom` (1,1), `position_smoothing_enabled` false, `process_callback` 1 (IDLE), `ignore_rotation` true. `Window.min_size` can be set and read back (1280x720).
35	- **Sizing and transform arithmetic.** A container with `stretch = true`, `stretch_shrink = 3` and size 1920x1080 sizes its viewport 640x360; `stretch_shrink = 7` on 3840x2160 gives 548x308 (floor), so `stretch_shrink` cannot reach `picture / k_z` at every ladder step. A container with `stretch = false` takes its viewport's size (640x360) and a `scale` of (3,3) gives a `get_global_transform` scale of exactly 3. A `CanvasLayer.scale` of (3,3) gives a child `Control` a `get_global_transform_with_canvas` scale of exactly 3 with the root `get_final_transform` identity (H not equal to k works from script). Under pass B, a `SubViewport` of 1920x1080 with `size_2d_override` 640x360 and `size_2d_override_stretch = true` has a stretch and final transform scale of exactly (3,3); a viewport of 1366x768 with an override of 682x384 has (2.002933, 2.0): **the override must divide the viewport size exactly or the scale is not an integer**. With `size_2d_override_stretch = false` the stretch transform stays identity and only `get_visible_rect()` changes. Root `content_scale_mode = canvas_items`, `aspect = keep`, `stretch = integer`, `content_scale_size = (640,360)` gave `get_final_transform` scale (2,2) with offset (43,24) at 1366x768, (2,2) with (160,90) at 1600x900, (3,3) with (0,60) at 1920x1200, (3,3) with (320,0) at 2560x1080, (4,4) with (440,0) at 3440x1440, and `get_visible_rect` 640x360 in every case: root integer stretch is correct at the default step with H equal to k and nowhere else.
36	- **Process order.** `Node._process` ran in ascending `process_priority` (-100, -50, 0, 100, 1000) in one frame. This is the headless fact only; the release-export confirmation and the cross-node case with presentation are ADR-0001's spike KRN-LAT-02.
37	- **Not probed, and why.** `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` and `frame_post_draw` exist as signals but **never fired** in a four-frame headless run (no draw happens headless), so the hook's order against `process_priority` is **UNVERIFIED** and windowed-only. `RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_driver_name()` and `get_current_rendering_method()` read `opengl3` and `gl_compatibility` headless, so **every probe above ran under the Compatibility renderer**: CPU-side arithmetic and member existence carry over, drawing behaviour does not.
38	
39	## ADR Dependencies
40	
41	| Field | Value |
42	|-------|-------|
43	| **Depends On** | ADR-0001 (the `ProcessPriority` constants, `PresentationClock`, and `present_time` ownership handed to the pipeline root; Proposed). |
44	| **Enables** | ADR-0009 (presentation subscriber contract: placement and the `frame_pre_draw` boundary), ADR-0028 (lighting budget: the renderer, driver, `use_hdr_2d` and the zoom-independent light rule), ADR-0030 (UI framework: HUD scale, layer 3 split, reading-face rasterisation), ADR-0034 (PROJECTOR: the camera limits rectangle is consumed here), ADR-0019 (Input Adapter: zoom actions call the pipeline, cursor mapping), every Pipeline, Lighting, HUD, Chart Table and Instruments story. |
45	| **Blocks** | Epics: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (the GDD names this ADR the first implementation-story gate: `world_to_hud`, `RESCALING`, the `get_final_transform` criteria), 2D Lighting & Occlusion (renderer and driver), HUD & Suit Layer (layer 2 and H). |
46	| **Ordering Note** | **Do not Accept** until (a) the lighting spike has run steps 1, 2 and 9 (renderer, driver, pass, Compatibility parity) and pipeline spike step 11 has passed, because § 1 and § 4 are provisional until then, and (b) ADR-0001 is Accepted. **Forward references (not yet written, not blocking authorship):** ADR-0009 owns what presentation may read and write and the Y-sort and z-band contract (this ADR only fixes where the world canvas and the camera write live); ADR-0010 owns the `src/` tree, the lint tool and which of § 5.5's rules are regex, boot-walk or runtime counters; ADR-0004 owns the dirty-key and notification transport (this ADR relies only on "a notification marks dirty, drawing happens later"); ADR-0006 owns where the display settings are persisted (a PROFILE value); ADR-0007 owns the tuning-table loader that carries `ZOOM_MIN_K`. |
47	
48	## Context
49	
50	### Problem Statement
51	The game's whole visual promise is that base pixels are square, unblurred and never at a fractional transform, and that "when the ship is still, the screen is still". The Pipeline GDD states the rules and defers the wiring to this ADR in six places: how a world viewport reaches the window size (pass B), how it reaches `picture / k_z` (every zoom step), how the HUD draws at `H` different from `k` under one root (mandatory on the Steam Deck from MVP), where the container's material slot and the camera write live, what hook the camera writes in, and what the renderer and Windows driver are. The Lighting GDD and the architecture add two more gates: the renderer method (Forward+ versus Compatibility) and the Windows driver (Direct3D 12 versus Vulkan), and one table for the draw-call budget (architecture IC-6), which today exists only as per-system figures. Until this ADR lands no Pipeline implementation story can start, and Lighting, HUD and Chart Table each build against different assumptions about the viewport stack.
52	
53	### Constraints
54	- **Integer scales only, pixel integrity first** (PR-1, PR-4): no scale anywhere in the world or the HUD is non-integer; the only non-integer text is the chart table's vector reading face (7.1).
55	- **Two integer scales in one window from MVP** (PR-12): Deck 1280x800 is world 2x, HUD 3x.
56	- **The simulation is untouched** (ADR-0001, kernel H9): nothing here reads or writes a state block; `k`, `H` and `k_z` are presentation state, never saved, never hashed.
57	- **One interpolator, no engine physics interpolation** (PR-4 rule 8): `physics_interpolation` stays off; the camera is a direct write, not a `Camera2D` scroll.
58	- **No autoload, no global** (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`, ADR-0001): geometry reaches consumers through an injected object, not a singleton.
59	- **Headless CI draws nothing** (`commands.test` runs `--headless`): the geometry is a pure function testable without a window; pixel-level checks are windowed and manual with retained evidence until a windowed runner exists (Pipeline "Gaps", Open Question 22).
60	- **Reference machines and build** (`project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`, ruling R12): RM-DESKTOP is a GTX 1050 Ti / RX 570 class machine at 1920x1080, "Vulkan 1.2+", P99 CPU frame ceiling 16.6 ms; RM-DECK is a Steam Deck LCD at 1280x800 with a 30 fps target and a 33.3 ms ceiling; every wall-clock figure is a Godot 4.7.2 release export, renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, 120-frame warm-up, P99 at most 90 % of the ceiling.
61	- **Engine reference silent** on `SubViewport` 2D sizing, override stretch, `use_hdr_2d`, `Light2D` under them and `frame_pre_draw`; the probes above settle sizes and arithmetic only.
62	
63	### Requirements
64	- A viewport stack in which the world is the only lit layer and the HUD, menus, hold plate and debug overlay are structurally outside world light, glow, the Filter and the camera jolt.
65	- A single writer for every viewport size, scale, offset and the camera transform, and a single caller of `HudLayout`.
66	- One re-derivation path for every cause of change (window resize, display mode, zoom step, setting change), completed inside one frame.
67	- Zoom by logical size, with `Camera2D.zoom` and `Control.scale` pinned at (1,1) everywhere they could be tempting.
68	- A render-mode flag with identical logical output in both modes, and a coordinate, sort, camera and HUD contract that does not mention which mode is live.
69	- A renderer-and-driver decision that names its gate and its reversal cost.
70	- One draw-call and timing table that nests the per-system figures and says who owns each row.
71	- A startup check that fails loudly in a dev build on any wrong effective value, and that can run in CI without a window.
72	
73	## Decision
74	
75	Five numbered sub-decisions, each reviewable alone: **§ 1 renderer method and Windows driver**, **§ 2 the viewport stack and scale wiring**, **§ 3 geometry, `k`, `H`, aspect and zoom**, **§ 4 render mode A and B**, **§ 5 project pins and startup guard rails**. Two shorter ones follow because other ADRs cite them: **§ 6 the camera write hook, frame order and `present_time`**, and **§ 7 the single draw-call and timing budget table**.
76	
77	### 1. Renderer method and Windows driver
78	
79	**Decision (provisional, pinned, spike-reversible).**
80	- **Method: Forward+** (`rendering/renderer/rendering_method = "forward_plus"`, already in `project.godot`). Compatibility and Mobile are assumed nowhere.
81	- **Windows driver: Vulkan** (`rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = "vulkan"`), and the Linux / Steam Deck driver is Vulkan (`driver.linuxbsd = "vulkan"`). Direct3D 12 is the recorded alternative.
82	- **The driver is never left to the engine default.** The probed built-in default is `vulkan`, but the reference says the 4.6 default is D3D12, and either could be the value a later 4.7.x patch or a new-project template writes. Because the editor drops a key whose value equals its default on save, the key may be absent from `project.godot`; the pin is therefore an **effective-value assertion** at startup (§ 5.3): a dev build halts when the printed driver is not the expected one, a release build logs it to the diagnostics header and continues. A choice of D3D12 later is written explicitly and changes the expected value in one constant.
83	
84	**Why Forward+.** The Lighting GDD's ambient floor, glow and `hdr_2d` model (steps 7 and 8 of the spike) assume a float 2D framebuffer and the 4.6 glow-before-tonemapping behaviour; the art bible sets `hdr_2d` for exactly that reason, and the training-knowledge claim that `use_hdr_2d` is a Forward+ and Mobile feature (not available in Compatibility) is **UNVERIFIED** and must be settled by lighting spike step 9. The reference cost of Forward+ is the Vulkan-class requirement, which both reference machines state (RM-DESKTOP "Vulkan 1.2+", the Deck). Compatibility remains the **reversible fallback** the Lighting GDD keeps open (step 9); a reversal re-opens `use_hdr_2d`, the glow and ambient design, shader support for the five-material cap, and the pass-B figures of § 7, and re-runs the spike, so it is a decision for the technical director, not a settings flip.
85	
86	**Why Vulkan on Windows.** (a) RM-DESKTOP is specified in Vulkan terms and RM-DECK is Vulkan, so one driver family produces the numbers the budget table is judged on and any driver-specific rendering difference (shader variants, glow, float framebuffers) is found once. (b) The reference gives D3D12's reason as "better driver compatibility", which concerns old and integrated GPUs below the minimum specification; it does not apply to a GTX 1050 Ti or RX 570 class card. (c) The installed binary's built-in default is Vulkan. (d) The D3D12 backend is the newer one (UNVERIFIED stability on 4.7.2); the cost of choosing the older backend is nothing at this tier. **Tie-break rule recorded for the spike:** switch to D3D12 only if lighting spike steps 1 and 2 on RM-DESKTOP show Vulkan failing a correctness check (palette-exact fills, hard cone edge, glow) that D3D12 passes, or D3D12 beating Vulkan's P99 CPU frame time by 10 % or more on the same scene; record both numbers either way. HDR output is off (§ 5), so the one Windows feature that might favour D3D12 is not used at MVP.
87	
88	**What gates it.** Lighting spike step 1 (print the driver name and rendering method and whether `hdr_2d` is honoured), step 2 (pass A/B), step 9 (Compatibility parity) and pipeline spike step 11. This section's status is therefore "provisional until those four have run", independent of the rest of the ADR.
89	
90	### 2. The viewport stack and scale wiring (wiring candidate (i), refined)
91	
92	**Decision.** The root `Window` runs with **stretch disabled**. Every scale in the window is chosen by script and is an integer by construction. One node, the **`PipelineRoot`**, is the only writer of the world viewport's size, override, scale, offset and canvas transform, of every `CanvasLayer` transform, and the only caller of `HudLayout`.
93	
94	```
95	root Window  (content_scale_mode = DISABLED, content_scale_factor = 1.0, min_size = 1280x720, clear colour black)
96	└─ PipelineRoot (Node; process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION; sole writer of everything below)
97	   ├─ WorldContainer: SubViewportContainer          layer 0   top-level Control on the root canvas
98	   │    stretch = false · mouse_filter = IGNORE · mouse_target = false · texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST (1)
99	   │    position = world_rect.position (integer valued) · scale = (k_z, k_z) under pass A, (1, 1) under pass B
100	   │    material = null at MVP (the single Filter hook, § 2.4)
101	   │    └─ WorldViewport: SubViewport                     size, override, hdr, snap, filter: § 2.2
102	   │         └─ the body frame: floors, Y-sorted layer, caps, lights, occluders, fringe, dust, horrors, web, instruments
103	   │             (the camera host writes this viewport's canvas_transform, § 6)
104	   ├─ HoldLayer     CanvasLayer  layer = 1   one opaque #000000 quad, only in TRANSIT_HOLD and BOOTING / LOADING
105	   ├─ HudLayer      CanvasLayer  layer = 2   group "hud"; scale = (H, H); offset = hud_rect.position
106	   │    └─ HudRoot: Control, size = hud_rect.size / H (fractional allowed), Control.scale = (1, 1)
107	   ├─ MenuPixelLayer   CanvasLayer layer = 3   scale = (H, H)   bitmap-face chart table and menus
108	   ├─ MenuReadingLayer CanvasLayer layer = 3   scale = (1, 1)   reading-face text, sizes in screen px (§ 2.5)
109	   └─ DebugLayer    CanvasLayer  layer = 4   scale = (H, H)   dev builds only; absent from release exports
110	```
111	
112	**2.1 Why this wiring (what the probes show).** Root integer stretch gave exactly `(k, k)` with the correct centring offset at every window tried, but only for the **default step with `H` equal to `k`**: its single scale applies to everything under the root, so a HUD at 3x over a 2x world, or a world at `picture / k_z`, would need a second, non-integer multiplier (the double-scale hazard of PR-7, candidate (ii)). With stretch disabled, a `CanvasLayer.scale` of (3,3) gave a child `Control` an exact scale of 3 with the root transform identity, and a `scale` of (3,3) on a `stretch = false` container gave an exact scale of 3; so the Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x are two independent integers chosen from script. `stretch_shrink` floors (3840/7 gives 548) and is an integer divisor of the container size, so candidate (iii) cannot reach `picture / k_z` at every step and is rejected as the primary; it remains the recorded fallback for the default step only (Alternative 2).
113	
114	**2.2 The world viewport members the root sets explicitly (every value is the probed built-in default's opposite or must not be inherited).**
115	- `size`: under pass A `field_px` (the logical size in base px, § 3); under pass B `world_rect.size` (`field_px * k_z`). **Never the 512x512 default and never the window size.** A scene that finds `size == (512, 512)` fails the scene-tree lint.
116	- `size_2d_override` and `size_2d_override_stretch`: unset (0,0) and `false` under pass A; `field_px` and `true` under pass B. **The override must divide the size exactly** (probed: 1366x768 over 682x384 gives a scale of 2.002933), which § 3 guarantees by sizing the viewport as `field_px * k_z`.
117	- `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (0); `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = true`; `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel = true` (belt and braces; placement is by integer write, ADR-0009); `use_hdr_2d = true` **provisional** (Lighting needs it; never set on the root viewport, which stays SDR-exact for the 4.6 palette, § 5.1); `use_debanding = false`; `transparent_bg = false`; `handle_input_locally = false` (the world has no `Control`; the effect of this member under a container that forwards no mouse events is UNVERIFIED, step 11, and the member may be left at its default if it proves irrelevant); `render_target_update_mode`: `UPDATE_ALWAYS` in `PRESENTING`, `TRANSIT_HOLD` with something to show and `RESCALING`; `UPDATE_DISABLED` in `PAUSED_FROZEN` and `HIDDEN`, with `UPDATE_ONCE` forced on the frame of any `RESCALING` that happens while updates are disabled, then back to `UPDATE_DISABLED` (PR-9). Whether a disabled viewport's last texture is held (not cleared) is UNVERIFIED and checked at step 11 with a resize while paused.
118	- **Nearest filtering is set in three places, with two differently numbered enums**: the project default (`default_texture_filter = 0`), the world viewport member above (`Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`, value 0), and `SubViewportContainer.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (value 1; the probed default is 0 = `PARENT_NODE`, which would inherit and blur the pass-A upscale). Mipmaps are off on every drawn sheet (art bible 8.4). `TileSet.tile_size` is 48x48 and set explicitly on every tile set.
119	
120	**2.3 Layers and what is structurally excluded.** The HUD (2), menus (3), hold plate (1) and debug overlay (4) are `CanvasLayer`s on the **root** viewport; world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the Filter material on the container and the camera transform live in the world viewport or on the container below them and cannot reach them (PR-3, HR-1, HR-6, HR-13). Nothing that must mix with world light may live above layer 0 (it goes in the world); a `Control` found under the world `SubViewport` fails the scene-tree lint, which is a build gate (HUD HS-2). Layers 2 to 4 are **never dimmed, blurred or desaturated** by pause.
121	
122	**2.4 The single full-screen hook.** The `SubViewportContainer.material` slot is the pipeline's only full-screen hook (PR-10): assigned and nulled **only** by `PipelineRoot.set_filter_material(material: ShaderMaterial)`, colour-writing only (a policy the Filter owns; the pipeline cannot inspect a shader), drawn below every `CanvasLayer`, receiving the world at screen resolution under both passes. **At MVP the slot is null** and the pipeline publishes `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`, `slot = NOT_USED` as a normal state, not an error (TR-pxl-023, TR-percfilter-030). The truth-channel mask route is a VS-A option that this ADR does not pre-build.
123	
124	**2.5 Two integer scales and text.** The HUD canvas is `HudRoot`, a `Control` of size `hud_rect.size / H` at the HUD layer's offset; every HUD element anchors to it, `HudLayout` outputs integer HUD-px rectangles relative to it, and `world_to_hud` returns coordinates in its space (PR-12, HUD HS-9). `Control.scale` stays (1,1) on every HUD node and no node animates scale or rotation. **Reading-face text is never drawn under an integer-scaled layer**: the chart table's reading face lives on `MenuReadingLayer` (scale (1,1)), whose labels set their font size to `round(base_size * scale_pct * window_scale)` and whose sizes are in screen px, while its pixel-grid face lives on the sibling `MenuPixelLayer` (scale `H`). Two `CanvasLayer` siblings may share the index 3 (probed: `layer` is a plain int; ordering between equal indices is by tree order, UNVERIFIED and checked at step 11, with `MenuReadingLayer` ordered after `MenuPixelLayer`).
125	
126	**2.6 One writer, enforced.** Only `PipelineRoot` (and its `ViewportWiring` helper) may write: `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override*`, the container's `position`, `scale`, `stretch_shrink` and `material`, any `CanvasLayer.scale` / `offset` / `transform`, `HudRoot.size`, and the world viewport's `canvas_transform`. Presentation subscribers (the Filter, Lighting, HUD, Chart Table) call neither; they receive a read-only `RenderLayout` (§ 3) and `world_to_hud`.
127	
128	### 3. Geometry: `k`, `H`, aspect, zoom, and one `RESCALING` path
129	
130	**Decision.** All derived geometry is one **pure function**, `RenderLayout.derive(...)`, a `RefCounted` value with no scene-tree dependency, injected where read. It implements the GDD's Formulas D.1 to D.5 and D.14 as written (the GDD owns the formulas; this ADR owns where their outputs go). `PipelineRoot` is the only caller that applies a result.

130	**Decision.** All derived geometry is one **pure function**, `RenderLayout.derive(...)`, a `RefCounted` value with no scene-tree dependency, injected where read. It implements the GDD's Formulas D.1 to D.5 and D.14 as written (the GDD owns the formulas; this ADR owns where their outputs go). `PipelineRoot` is the only caller that applies a result.
131	
132	- **Inputs:** the window pixel size `W x H_w` (physical pixels, never DPI-scaled; `content_scale_factor` stays 1.0), a `DisplaySettings` value (aspect `KEEP | EXPAND`, manual world scale `0` for Auto, HUD scale choice), the current zoom step `k_z`, the static `ZOOM_MIN_K` table, and the `offered(P_w, P_h)` subset of HUD scales from `HudLayout` (HUD owns the predicate `bottom_row_fit`).
133	- **Outputs (all integers or integer-valued):** `k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H_w/360))` (a window below `min_size` 1280x720 cannot occur on a compliant window manager; if one does, `k_auto` is clamped to the Section G invariant `k_min == 2` and a `WINDOW_BELOW_MIN` diagnostics entry is written, never a `k` of 1 or 0), `k_base` (manual `k` when below Auto, else `k_auto`; a manual `k` below Auto forces `KEEP`), `H` (`H_default = max(k_auto, 3)`, never below 3, in `[H_default, 2 * H_default]` and in `offered`), `field_px` (D.1/D.3 at `k_base`, D.5 at a ladder step), `picture_rect` (the window region that shows the game, centred, integer), `world_rect = field_px * k_z` centred in the picture (a ladder field that does not divide the picture leaves a few black pixels; the HUD does not move), `hud_rect` (**pinned to the `k_base` picture rect**, so a zoom step never moves the HUD), `hud_canvas = hud_rect.size / H`.
134	- **Letterbox bars** are the root viewport's **clear colour** (`default_clear_color = (0,0,0,1)`, § 5.1), outside every node, so the Filter, the jolt and any `CanvasLayer` cannot touch them. A 1-HUD-px hairline at the picture edge, if the art director adds one, is a layer-1 element excluded from the HUD count (PR-12 resolution).
135	
136	**3.1 Zoom is a change of logical size, never `Camera2D.zoom`.** The ladder is `[effective_min, k_base + 2]` with `effective_min = ZOOM_MIN_K(k_base, target class)` (default 1 until the spike fills it); `k_z` is persistent, edge-triggered, never held and never saved. `PipelineRoot.request_zoom_step(direction: int)` is the only entry point (the Input Adapter calls it from its `_process`; ADR-0019). A step is accepted when it is inside the ladder, no other step was accepted this frame, and at least `ZOOM_STEP_MIN_INTERVAL` (0.15 s) of **engine process time** has passed since the last accepted step; the interval is a countdown decremented by the `_process` delta in `PipelineRoot`, **not** `present_time` (frozen under pause, where zoom must still work) and not any `Time.*` call (forbidden by ADR-0001's clock lint); surplus presses are discarded, not queued, and counted in `diag.zoom_step_rate_limited`. A refused press (beyond either end, or below `ZOOM_MIN_K`, or while the camera is `HELD`) increments `diag.zoom_step_refused` with a reason. Accepting a step sets the layout dirty, so the step is **one `RESCALING` frame and a camera cut**: under pass A `SubViewport.size = field_px(k_z)` and `container.scale = k_z`; under pass B `size = field_px * k_z`, `override = field_px`. Lighting has no zoom handler: every `Light2D` length is in base px and independent of `k_z` under both passes (LO-16), which this wiring honours because the world canvas is never scaled by `Camera2D`.
137	
138	**3.2 One `RESCALING` path for every cause.** `Window.size_changed`, a zoom step, a display-mode change, a world-scale or HUD-scale or aspect setting change, and `dpi_changed` each **only set a dirty flag** (the same dirty-mark principle as every notification). `PipelineRoot._process` re-derives at most once per rendered frame, before that frame is drawn (the main loop processes events, then `_process`, then draws), so a continuous drag of the window edge is a sequence of at most one re-derivation per frame converging on the final size (coalescing by frame, not by time). The re-derivation:
139	1. computes the new `RenderLayout`;
140	2. **reallocates the viewport only if `field_px`, `k_z` or the render mode's size changed**; a pure translation (the picture re-centring by a pixel during a drag) moves only the container position and the HUD rect;
141	3. applies it through `ViewportWiring` (container position and scale, viewport size and override, layer offsets and scales, `HudRoot.size`), calls `HudLayout` once, re-derives the camera limits rectangle consumed by the solver, and republishes `world_to_hud`'s inputs;
142	4. forces `UPDATE_ONCE` if updates were disabled (§ 2.2);
143	5. enters the `RESCALING` state for that frame and `PRESENTING` (or the held state) on the next.
144	The re-derivation completes inside the frame and costs at most 4 ms CPU (§ 7). No frame shows a fractional transform because there is none to show: every transform written is integer-valued.

206	### 6. The camera write hook, frame order and `present_time`
207	
208	**6.1 The camera is a pure solver behind a host (TR-pxl-010, 011, 012, 013, 015; the formulas D.6 to D.10 are the GDD's).** `CameraSolver` is a `RefCounted` with `solve(input: SolverInput, state: SolverState, params: SolverParams) -> Pose`, no scene-tree dependency, float64 per-axis state held as scalars (not `Vector2`), `dt` clamped to `DT_MAX` (0.05 s). The **type of `SolverInput` is the enforcement of Camera C1**: it carries only the follow target's previous and current body-local positions, `tick_alpha`, the raw local beam aim, the zoom step, `dt`, and cut / rebase flags; it has no field through which Attention, breach, horrors, sound, the graph or sanity could enter, so the same input trace gives the same camera trace in calm, tell and breach by construction. The Perception Filter has no write path to a camera or viewport property (§ 2.6). Solver parameters and `ZOOM_MIN_K` are tuning tables loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline and injected. Camera state is never persisted: the host resets (`CUT`) the solver on every `LOADING → RUNNING` and every pod or transit body transfer, starting with `L = 0` easing in; a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` calls `rebase(frame_delta_px)`, which shifts the follow and history and keeps lag and `L`. Owners of moving read views set `previous := current` in `post_restore` (ADR-0016), so the first frame after a restore interpolates nothing.
209	
210	**6.2 The hook.** The camera host (a top-level presentation node under `PipelineRoot`, never a child of a body) writes the world viewport's `canvas_transform` **directly**, once per frame, from `pose_q` plus the jolt offset, in a handler connected to **`RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`**, after every presentation node has written its position in its own `_process` (ADR-0009). The handler does this and the parallax layer offsets (`layer.position = -floor(pose_q * scroll_scale)` whole base px) and nothing else. **Primary variant: no `Camera2D` in the world tree** (a lint); the transform has scale (1,1), no rotation and no skew every frame and only the host writes it. **Alternative variant**, if the direct write is rejected at step 12: a `Camera2D` with `anchor_mode = ANCHOR_MODE_FIXED_TOP_LEFT` (probed: `anchor_mode` default 1 is `DRAG_CENTER`), drag margins off, and `force_update_scroll()` called after each write; every camera assertion is read as holding on the `Camera2D` if the variant has one. `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at the engine defaults in both variants; **the solver is the only clamp** against the limits rectangle a PROJECTOR sets (ADR-0034), so `world_to_hud` is never offset while `CLAMPED`. A `Camera2D` never descends from a physics body.
211	- **What is UNVERIFIED:** that `frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` of the frame and before the frame's draw, and that a `canvas_transform` written there is the one drawn (probed: the signal exists and does not fire headless). **Fallback and trigger:** if step 11/12 shows any `_process` running after the handler, or a one-frame disagreement between camera and sprite, the host's write moves to the `_process` of `PipelineRoot` at a priority later than every presentation node. ADR-0001's three constants have no such value, so this requires **adding `PRESENTATION_LATE` to `ProcessPriority` (an additive amendment to ADR-0001, requested in Open Question OQ-D)**; until then a literal priority is forbidden and the fallback is not built.
212	- **Scope edge with ADR-0009.** The Pipeline GDD PR-8 item 3 calls the pipeline root's `frame_pre_draw` handler the "render callback" in which every subscriber reads and draws. That is **not** adopted here: subscribers draw from their own `_process` at `PRESENTATION` (the shape architecture § Presentation subscriber contract shows) and `frame_pre_draw` is reserved for the camera host's one write, so a subscriber's draw never depends on a signal whose ordering is unverified. ADR-0009 owns the subscriber side; this is returned as a GDD sync item.
213	
214	**6.3 `present_time`, the pipeline-owned clock (ADR-0001 handed the owner to this ADR).** `PipelineRoot` owns `present_time: float` (seconds, a 64-bit float). It advances by the `_process` delta while the kernel is `RUNNING`, `SAVING` or `LOADING` with the hold shown, is frozen while `PAUSED`, and is **never scaled by reduced motion** (reduced motion scales individual effects). Layer 0 animation uses only `present_time`; layers 3 and 4 run on engine process time so the chart table responds while paused; the HUD (layer 2) freezes with the world. The cosmetic-phase rule ("the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase") is ADR-0001's and is not restated. The pipeline reads the kernel's state (`RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING`, `FAULTED`) through a read-only kernel-state accessor on the facet the composition root gives it; `PresentationClock` as ADR-0001 defines it carries only `running`, so Cross-ADR Assumption A2 asks ADR-0009 (or an ADR-0001 amendment) for the full state. `SceneTree.paused` is not the kernel's pause and is not used by the pipeline.

345	### Implementation Guidelines
346	- **Must** keep the root `Window` at `content_scale_mode = DISABLED`, `content_scale_factor = 1.0`, `min_size = (1280, 720)`; **must never** enable root stretch or `canvas_items` scaling to obtain `k`, `H` or `k_z`.
347	- **Must** route every write of `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override*`, the container's `position`, `scale`, `stretch_shrink` and `material`, any `CanvasLayer` `scale` / `offset` / `transform`, `HudRoot.size` and the world `canvas_transform` through `PipelineRoot` and `ViewportWiring`; **must never** write them from a presentation subscriber, the Filter, Lighting, the HUD or the Chart Table.
348	- **Must** compute all geometry in `RenderLayout.derive` from the window's **pixel** size and apply a result only in `PipelineRoot._process`; **must never** derive `k`, `H`, `world_to_hud` or the cursor mapping anywhere else, never read `DisplayServer` DPI for `k`, and never test `device == 0` for the cursor.
349	- **Must** size the world viewport as `field_px` (pass A) or `field_px * k_z` (pass B) with `size_2d_override` equal to `field_px`; **must never** leave the 512x512 default, size it to the window, or set an override that does not divide the size exactly.
350	- **Must** implement zoom by changing logical size and the container scale; **must never** set `Camera2D.zoom`, tween a scale, or write `Control.scale` on any HUD node, and **must never** apply a non-integer scale to the world container or a HUD layer.
351	- **Must** set NEAREST in all three places (project default, world viewport member, container `texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`), keep mipmaps off on drawn sheets, set `SubViewport.size` and `TileSet.tile_size` (48x48) explicitly, and set the world viewport's snap and HDR members in code.
352	- **Must** keep the HUD, menus, hold plate and debug overlay in `CanvasLayer`s on the root viewport; **must never** place a `Control` or a HUD node under the world `SubViewport`, and **must never** put reading-face text under an integer-scaled layer.
353	- **Must** treat `Window.size_changed`, zoom presses and setting changes as dirty marks and re-derive at most once per frame; **must never** re-derive inside the signal handler, and never queue surplus zoom presses.
354	- **Must** use the engine `_process` delta (not `present_time`, not `Time.*`) for the zoom cooldown; **must** use `present_time` for all layer-0 animation.
355	- **Must** write the camera only by `canvas_transform` in the `frame_pre_draw` handler (primary) and only from `CameraHost`; **must never** add a `Camera2D` to the world tree in the primary variant, set `Camera2D.limit_*`, parent a camera to a body, or let any module other than the pipeline root or the camera host write a camera or viewport property.
356	- **Must** keep `SolverInput` free of any world-state field; **must never** pass Attention, breach, horror, sound, graph or sanity values to the solver.
357	- **Must** assert the pinned configuration at startup through `StartupCheck` over a `RenderConfigSnapshot` (a pure function that returns findings); **must never** `assert`, `push_error` or `quit` inside the check, and **must** report the renderer and driver rows NOT ASSESSED under a headless display server.
358	- **Must** read `RENDER_MODE` only inside `ViewportWiring`; **must never** branch on it in any other class.
359	- **Must** change a draw-call or timing figure only by amending § 7; **must** read draw calls per viewport with `get_render_info`; **must never** infer the HUD's count from the frame total.

360	- **Must** pin the renderer and driver as in § 1 and record the printed driver name with every performance result; **must never** rely on the engine default driver.
361	- **Should** unit-test `RenderLayout.derive` against every row of PR-1's table (including 1365x768 and 3440x1440), the zoom ladder and `ZOOM_MIN_K` clamping, and `world_to_hud` / `mouse_to_world_aim` as pure functions with no window.
362	
363	## Alternatives Considered
364	
365	### Alternative 1: Root integer stretch plus script-set container size (candidate (ii))
366	- **Description**: Keep `canvas_items` / `integer` stretch on the root so the engine computes `k` and the centring offset, and drive the world `SubViewport.size` from script.
367	- **Pros**: the engine does the default-step arithmetic (probed: exact `(k, k)` and correct offsets at every window); fewer values for the pipeline to compute.
368	- **Cons**: the single root scale multiplies everything under it, so a HUD at `H` different from `k` and a world at `picture / k_z` need a second multiplier on top of the stretch: the double-scale hazard, with effective scales that become products and, off the default step, floats. The cursor needs the inverse final transform. The Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x, an MVP requirement, cannot be integers.
369	- **Rejection Reason**: it is correct only at `H = k` and the default zoom (probed), which the Deck violates on day one.
370	
371	### Alternative 2: `SubViewportContainer.stretch = true` with `stretch_shrink`
372	- **Description**: Let the container size the viewport (`stretch_shrink = k` on a screen-pixel-sized container, or on a base-unit container under root stretch, candidate (iii)).
373	- **Pros**: no script-set scale on the container; the integer lives in an int property; probed to size the viewport correctly (shrink 3 on 1920x1080 gives 640x360).
374	- **Cons**: `stretch_shrink` floors (3840/7 gives 548x308), so a ladder step is not always `picture / k_z`; the container, not the pipeline root, then writes `SubViewport.size`, which weakens the single-writer rule (TR-pxl-003); under root stretch it does not reach `H` different from `k`.
375	- **Rejection Reason**: not adopted as the primary. It is the recorded fallback if step 11 shows that a scaled `stretch = false` container mis-samples or bleeds, with the single-writer rule restated for the container's `stretch_shrink` (`PipelineRoot` still writes it and asserts the resulting viewport size).
376	
377	### Alternative 3: Fractional stretch with a sharpening filter, or `Camera2D.zoom`
378	- **Description**: Scale the whole picture by `min(W/640, H/360)` and sharpen; or zoom with `Camera2D.zoom`.
379	- **Pros**: fills every window; no letterbox; the simplest wiring.
380	- **Cons**: breaks the 1 px contour, 2 px band and 2 px fringe widths (art bible 5.6); a non-integer `Camera2D.zoom` is exactly the fractional transform the pipeline exists to forbid; `Camera2D.zoom` shares the unresolved wiring question and has no pixel-snap member.
381	- **Rejection Reason**: rejected by PR-1 and PR-4 rule 4 before this ADR; recorded so a later change of mind meets the reasons.
382	
383	### Alternative 4: Compatibility renderer (or Mobile) instead of Forward+
384	- **Description**: Use OpenGL 3.3 for the broadest hardware support and lower driver risk.
385	- **Pros**: runs on GPUs below Vulkan 1.2; the headless probe runs on it; cheap on integrated GPUs; no D3D12 / Vulkan driver choice at all.
386	- **Cons**: `use_hdr_2d` (and therefore the glow and the 0 to 1 % ambient floor the Lighting GDD designs around) is UNVERIFIED there and believed unavailable; Light2D, shadow and shader parity is the open lighting spike step 9; it is not the renderer the reference machines' build string names; it re-opens pass-B figures and the five-shader cap.
387	- **Rejection Reason**: not adopted; kept as the reversible fallback (§ 1) gated by lighting spike step 9. A reversal is a technical-director decision that re-runs the lighting spike.
388	
389	### Alternative 5: Direct3D 12 as the Windows driver
390	- **Description**: Follow the reference's stated 4.6 default.
391	- **Pros**: the engine's own default for Windows per the reference; better compatibility on old and integrated GPUs; HDR output may be easier on Windows (not used at MVP).
392	- **Cons**: the reference and the installed binary disagree about the default (OQ-C); the backend is newer; the Steam Deck cannot use it, so Windows and Deck numbers would differ in driver; RM-DESKTOP is specified in Vulkan terms; the compatibility benefit is for hardware below the minimum specification.
393	- **Rejection Reason**: not adopted as the default; the tie-break rule in § 1 switches to it on measured evidence.
394	
395	### Alternative 6: Pass B as the default, or the viewport sized to the window
396	- **Description**: Render lights, shadows and glow at window resolution (the art director's IDEAL), with the viewport at window size and an override.
397	- **Pros**: smooth interior falloff of the beam; edges 1 to 2 screen px wide.
398	- **Cons**: up to 9x the lit pixels at 1080p (2.07 M vs 0.23 M) and 22 MB of render target against 3 MB; at the bottom ladder step A already costs the same; an override that does not divide the window gives a non-integer scale (probed); rotated segments are off the grid.
399	- **Rejection Reason**: A is the default and the art-director's accepted fallback; B stays behind the flag and is adopted only if it fits 16.6 ms. The window-sized viewport is rejected outright for the picture-sized one (§ 4).
400	
401	### Alternative 7: HUD inside the world viewport with unshaded materials, or a global `RenderLayout` autoload
402	- **Description**: Draw the HUD in the world viewport unshaded; or expose `k`, `H` and the layout through an autoload.
403	- **Pros**: one viewport; trivial access.
404	- **Cons**: unshaded items still receive glow and the full-screen pass, making HR-1 a per-node discipline one forgotten material breaks (the GDD rejected it in PR-3); an autoload breaks registry `kernel_autoload_or_global` and headless tests that need several layouts at once.
405	- **Rejection Reason**: structural exclusion by viewport is the requirement; layout is injected as a value.
406	
407	## Consequences
408	
409	### Positive
410	- Every scale in the window is an integer chosen by one script, so the world and the HUD can be two different integers (the Deck) and the fractional-transform failure has nowhere to hide.
411	- Zoom, resize, mode change and setting change are one `RESCALING` path; the geometry is a pure function testable headless against every window in PR-1's table.
412	- The HUD, menus, hold plate and debug overlay cannot receive world light, glow, the Filter or the jolt, by viewport, not by discipline.
413	- A and B differ in one class; the identical-output test is a unit test.
414	- The renderer and driver are pinned, asserted by effective value, and reversible by a named spike result with a named cost.
415	- The draw-call and timing figures are one nested table with owners, the open-chart arithmetic is made explicit, and zoom-out steps are withheld rather than content cut.
416	- The cursor needs no inverse final transform, and the HUD no root stretch.
417	
418	### Negative
419	- The pipeline computes centring, the HUD rect and the letterbox itself instead of getting them from the engine's stretch (a few lines of pure arithmetic, tested against the engine's probed offsets).
420	- A scaled `stretch = false` container is a wiring not exercised by the engine's own templates; step 11 must prove its sampling and edge behaviour.
421	- A ladder field that does not divide the picture leaves a few black pixels inside it (D.5).
422	- Pass B costs memory and lit pixels and its viewport must be sized to the picture, not the window.
423	- The renderer and driver are provisional, so Lighting and the performance budgets are conditional until four spike steps have run.
424	- Two `CanvasLayer`s share index 3 and their relative order rests on tree order (UNVERIFIED).
425	- Headless CI cannot assert the renderer, the driver, draw calls or pixels; those are windowed and manual with retained evidence until a windowed runner exists.
426	- The camera hook depends on a signal whose order is unverified, and its fallback needs an additive ADR-0001 amendment.
427	
428	## Risks
429	- **`frame_pre_draw` fires before a late `_process`, or the written transform is not the one drawn.** Mitigation: step 11/12 test; the host's write moves to a late-priority `_process` (OQ-D); the camera is allowed to use the previous frame's pose in the meantime (ADR-0001 Risks).
430	- **A scaled container blurs, bleeds an edge pixel or ignores its `texture_filter`.** Mitigation: three-place NEAREST; step 11 screenshots the first frame after every resize and every ladder step; fallback Alternative 2.
431	- **The root default stretch or driver changes in a later 4.7.x patch or by a project-template re-save.** Mitigation: effective-value assertion plus the headless `project.godot` test; a key whose required value differs from the default is required in the file.
432	- **Forward+ or Vulkan turns out wrong on a reference machine.** Mitigation: the gate and tie-break in § 1; the reversal cost is stated; budgets are recorded with the printed driver.
433	- **Edge-drag resize allocates a viewport every frame.** Mitigation: reallocate only when `field_px` or `k_z` changes; translate otherwise; budget 4 ms; step 11 drags for 2 s.
434	- **Windows display scaling or `allow_hidpi` gives a window size that is not physical pixels.** Mitigation: `k` derived from the window pixel size only; step 11 logs it at 125 % and 150 %.
435	- **A subscriber writes a viewport property, or a `Control` slips under the world viewport.** Mitigation: the scene-tree lint is a build gate; the debug tree walk; the single-writer guideline (lint rules ADR-0010).
436	- **The draw-call table's open-chart row (92) is silently exceeded by a chart plate with the HUD drawn (102).** Mitigation: the row states the hidden-HUD rule; `DrawBudget.validate` fixture; OQ-F.
437	- **A misconfigured `project.godot` ships.** Mitigation: the dev halt, the release diagnostics header and the CI parse test with one-key-at-a-time fixtures.

483	| pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md | TR-pxl-027: flash safety clamps computed analytically from modifier state, no GPU readback in the clamp path | ADR-0028 | the table row for the dev-only flash scan cost is outside § 7's release figures |
484	
485	## Performance Implications
486	- **CPU**: `PipelineRoot._process` at most 0.5 ms P99 including the state machine and `world_to_hud` for 32 prompts; `CameraSolver.solve` at most 0.05 ms; the `RESCALING` re-derivation at most 4 ms, once per resize frame, with viewport reallocation only when `field_px` or `k_z` changes. All unmeasured until the release-export spike.
487	- **Memory**: world render targets at most 3 MB (A) or 22 MB (B) at 1080p, scaled by lit pixels at other targets (D.16). `RenderLayout` is a handful of integers per rederivation.
488	- **Load Time**: negligible; the pipeline root builds the stack in BOOTING step 2 before content loads. Shader Baker reduces first-frame hitching (measured by lighting spike step 10).
489	- **GPU**: the container composite at most 0.3 ms (1080p) and 1.0 ms (2160p). Pass A shades 230,400 lit pixels at the default field; at the bottom ladder step A costs the same as B (2,073,600 at 1080p).
490	- **Network**: none. Nothing here is replicated; each client has its own window and camera.
491	
492	## Migration Plan
493	No code exists. The current `project.godot` has only `renderer/rendering_method="forward_plus"` and a feature list; the pinned block of § 5.1 (every **required** row) is added by the first Pipeline story. **GDD and reference sync (items returned to the orchestrator, not applied by this ADR):**
494	- `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md`:
495	  - PR-7: under pass B the viewport is the picture (`field_px * k_z`), not the window; the override must divide the size exactly.
496	  - PR-15 (1)(2) and the Startup assertions criteria: stretch `mode = disabled`, `scale_mode = integer` required in the file, the assertion reads `DISABLED` plus the wiring readback; the HDR-output key name `display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output` and the debanding key are now sourced.
497	  - PR-7 and the scale criteria: replace `get_final_transform().get_scale()` by the readback chain of § 5.4.
498	  - PR-8 item 3: subscribers draw in their own `_process`; `frame_pre_draw` is the camera host's.
499	  - D.16: name the container composite draw call.
500	  - PR-3 versus art bible 8.4 on where `hdr_2d` is set.
501	- `chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md`: layer 3 is two sibling `CanvasLayer`s (pixel face at `H`, reading face at 1).
502	- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`: layer diagram platform row and § 8 step 1 mention "Forward+" and "stretch" as settled; they become provisional and `disabled`; OQ-2 points to this ADR.
503	- `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/rendering.md` (reference correction, suggested): the probed built-in `driver.windows` default is `vulkan`, which conflicts with the "D3D12 is the Windows default" line.
504	- `tests/unit/render/` (accepted by the GDD for the auto tests) holds the `RenderLayout`, `StartupCheck`, `DrawBudget` and `project.godot` parse tests; the windowed runner is a `/test-setup` item (Pipeline Open Question 22).
505	
506	## Validation Criteria
507	- **Spike step 11** passes: at every window in PR-1's table the readback chain gives exactly `(k_z, k_z)` and `(H, H)`, under pass A and pass B, on a dev build and a release export; the first frame after each resize, zoom step and mode change shows no fractional transform (retained screenshots); a 2 s edge drag produces no fractional frame and stays within the 4 ms `RESCALING` budget; 1365x768 shows true-black residual.
508	- **Unit tests (headless, no window):** `RenderLayout.derive` matches PR-1's table for every row including 1365x768, 1366x768, 2560x1080 and 3440x1440, centring offsets agree with the probed engine offsets (43,24), (160,90), (0,60), (320,0), (440,0); the ladder and `ZOOM_MIN_K` clamping; manual `k` below Auto forces `keep`; `H` choice is clamped to the offered subset; `world_to_hud` and `mouse_to_world_aim` examples from D.14 and D.14b; `StartupCheck` returns exactly one finding naming the key for a snapshot with one wrong value, per key; `DrawBudget.validate` on the table.
509	- **CI:** the `project.godot` parse test passes the shipped file and fails, naming the key, for each fixture with one required key removed or set wrong; the scene-tree lint finds zero violations; no `Camera2D` in the world tree (primary variant); no assignment to `Camera2D.zoom` outside the reset path; the dev-only files (Debug Overlay scene, tree-walk, flash-scan) are absent from the release export list.
510	- **Equivalence:** the same input trace under `RENDER_MODE = A` and `B` gives identical `k`, `H`, `k_z`, `pose_q` sequence, cut list, Y-sort order and `world_to_hud` outputs; only viewport size, memory and frame time differ.
511	- **Hook:** spike step 12 shows zero render-pixel disagreement between camera and sprite across 1,000 frames with `frame_pre_draw` as the write point, or the fallback is adopted and OQ-D is resolved.
512	- **Renderer and driver (gates acceptance):** lighting spike steps 1, 2 and 9 run on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK with the printed method and driver recorded; the tie-break rule of § 1 is applied to the measured numbers; the recorded choice replaces "provisional" in § 1.
513	- **Budgets:** the P99 table of § 7.3 and the per-viewport draw-call table of § 7.1 are measured on the release export on both machines with the driver name recorded; each withheld zoom step is written into `ZOOM_MIN_K`. Until then performance criteria are neither pass nor fail.
514	
515	## Related
516	- Depends on: ADR-0001 (Proposed).
517	- Forward references: ADR-0004 (change notification: dirty marks only), ADR-0006 (display settings persistence), ADR-0007 (tuning tables: `ZOOM_MIN_K`, solver parameters), ADR-0009 (presentation subscriber contract, placement, Y-sort), ADR-0010 (source layout, lint tool, which rules are regex or boot walk), ADR-0016 (`post_restore` order), ADR-0019 (Input Adapter: zoom actions, cursor), ADR-0028 (lighting budget: renderer consumer, flash-clamp ownership), ADR-0030 (UI framework: layer 3 split, reading face), ADR-0034 (PROJECTOR: camera limits rectangle).
518	- GDDs: `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` (PR-1 to PR-15, D.1 to D.16, States and Transitions, Performance budget); `2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md` (LO-16, spike table steps 1 to 10); `hud-and-suit-layer.md` (HS-2, HS-3, HS-9); `perception-filter.md` (PF-25, PF-26); `chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md` (CT-11, CT-13, CT-18, ASK-CT-12, `LAYER3_DRAW_CALL_BUDGET`); `failure-and-trail-system.md` (`D_FT_MAX`); `design/art/art-bible.md` 8.4, 8.6, 8.10, 8.12.
519	- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § Engine Knowledge Gap Summary, § Required ADRs, § Spikes that gate ADRs, OQ-2, IC-6; `docs/registry/architecture.yaml` (entries proposed by this ADR).
520	
521	## Open Questions
522	- **OQ-A.** Renderer method and Windows driver stay provisional until lighting spike steps 1, 2 and 9 and pipeline spike step 11 have run. Owner: the spike; the technical director rules on a reversal.
523	- **OQ-B.** Whether a scaled `stretch = false` `SubViewportContainer` samples with NEAREST and without an edge bleed under both passes, and whether `stretch_shrink` (Alternative 2) is the better primary. Spike step 11.
524	- **OQ-C.** Reference versus binary: the pinned reference says D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6; the installed 4.7.2 reports `driver.windows = vulkan` as its built-in. Which is the engine default for a new project versus for a project with no key is unresolved. The reference doc may need correction; this ADR avoids the question by pinning the effective value.
525	- **OQ-D.** The fallback camera write needs a `PRESENTATION_LATE` priority constant that ADR-0001's `ProcessPriority` does not define (its rule forbids a literal). An additive ADR-0001 amendment is requested if the spike does not confirm `frame_pre_draw`.
526	- **OQ-E.** Whether pipeline startup findings deserve a registered fault domain (ADR-0003's 15 to 31 range is reserved for presentation and tooling) or stay a pipeline-local value. ADR-0003 or ADR-0010 decides; this ADR needs neither.
527	- **OQ-F.** The container composite's own draw call is not a named term of D.16 (`D_filter` is 0 at MVP). If `get_render_info` on the root counts it, `D_root` closed is `60 + 1 + 1 + 1`; the spike reads it and the table is amended. Also, the open-chart cap of 92 rests on the HUD-hidden-under-plate rule; the GDDs should state it where the 92 is stated.
528	- **OQ-G.** Whether `UPDATE_DISABLED` holds the last texture across a resize (the GDD assumes it, with `UPDATE_ONCE` as the guard), and whether two `CanvasLayer`s at index 3 keep tree order. Spike step 11.
529	- **OQ-H.** The `use_hdr_2d` setting on the world viewport only, versus the art bible's project-level `hdr_2d = true`: lighting spike step 7 (ambient with and without HDR) decides; the art bible text needs the same correction as the GDD.
530	
531	## Review Log
532	- **2026-10-28 joint review (godot-specialist engine review and technical-director TD-ADR review).** Both reviews were unavailable for this ADR: the harness returned "review unavailable" for each, so no finding ids were issued and none were applied or declined.
533	  - Revision pass (autonomous, action "Revise flagged items"): no text in the ADR body was changed, because there was nothing flagged. The Proposed status, the registry candidates and the GDD sync items are unchanged from the original authoring.
534	  - Consequence: this ADR is NOT reviewed. Its engine-behaviour claims remain UNVERIFIED as stated in Last Verified, and OQ-A to OQ-H stay open. The joint review should be re-run before the ADR moves to Accepted; the review log will then list each finding id and its disposition, as ADR-0007's does.

176	### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages
177	
178	**A single `PresentationHost` node** (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code) owns a `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls `driver.frame(...)` from its `_process`. The host is the Pipeline root or a node it owns (ADR-0008 decides which; either way exactly one node). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.
179	
180	This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result that KRN-LAT-02 has not yet confirmed for a rendering build. Only the order **host after TickDriver** depends on ADR-0001's verified order.
181	
182	```gdscript
183	# src/presentation/presentation_stage.gd. Named constants only; nobody writes a literal stage number.
184	class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted
185	const PROJECT: int = 0         # PROJECTOR builds and rebuilds, chunked
186	const CAMERA_SOLVE: int = 1    # CameraSolver computes pose_q and world_to_hud; the canvas write is in frame_pre_draw
187	const AVATAR: int = 2          # Avatar Presenter: position, frame, flip, beam pose
188	const FILTER: int = 3          # Perception Filter step, decoy list, perceived() memo
189	const INSTRUMENTS: int = 4
190	const HUD: int = 5
191	const LIGHTING: int = 6        # reads the beam pose (AVATAR) and the decoy list (FILTER)
192	const TRAIL: int = 7           # Failure & Trail (truth channel, reads no Filter product)
193	const AUDIO: int = 8
194	const DEBUG: int = 9
195	```
196	
197	**The pinned partial order and why this total order satisfies it.** Every source that states an edge is satisfied:
198	- HUD AC-HS-89 and TR-hud-022: camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting. Stages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.
199	- PF-35 and TR-percfilter-025: Avatar, then Filter, then Lighting reads the decoy list. Stages 2, 3, 6.
200	- TR-pc-040: the Presenter's beam pose is written before Lighting applies. Stages 2, 6.
201	- Instruments call `perceived()`, so they follow the Filter. Stages 3, 4.
202	- The rest (Trail, Audio, Debug after Lighting) is a convention. It differs from the order in `architecture.md` § Data Flow (Avatar, Lighting, Trail, Instruments, HUD, Audio), which the three GDD-stated edges override; § GDD sync lists the rewrite.
203	- **Camera versus Avatar.** Pipeline C2 asks for the camera "ordered after the actor" so that both compose the same interpolated position. This ADR gets the same guarantee by construction, not by order: the solver and the Avatar Presenter both call `Placement.at` with the same `PresentFrame` values, so they cannot disagree. The solver runs first because the HUD needs `world_to_hud` before it draws (TR-hud-022). Step 12 of the pipeline spike (zero render-px disagreement) tests the claim.
204	
205	```gdscript
206	class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
207	var name: StringName
208	var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
209	var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
210	var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void
211	var on_discontinuity: Callable        # (kind: int) -> void; DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE or DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT
212	
213	class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
214	var alpha: float            # clock.tick_alpha read ONCE per frame; in [0, 1]; 1.0 while not RUNNING
215	var T: int                  # last committed tick; may feed values the simulation also computes, never cosmetic phase
216	var running: bool
217	var present_time: float     # supplied by the Pipeline root (ADR-0008); frozen while PAUSED; the only cosmetic clock
218	var render_delta: float     # for smoothing filters only; never a phase
219	
220	class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted
221	func register(desc: PresenterDescriptor) -> void          # BOOTING only
222	func freeze() -> void                                      # sorts by stage; checks reads < stage; unique names; fails boot otherwise
223	func frame(host_delta: float, present_time: float) -> void # fills PresentFrame, handles load_seq, runs the stages
224	func notify_camera_cut() -> void                           # called by the camera stage; next frame every presenter gets CAMERA_CUT
225	```
226	
227	`present` and `on_discontinuity` are registered `Callable`s returning `void`. They are **not** kernel-invoked owner callables, so ADR-0003's `CompletionToken` rule does not apply to them, and registering `Callable`s rather than overriding a base class avoids the 4.7 typed-return override rule altogether (ADR-0003 § 1 makes the same choice for owners). If ADR-0010 picks an `@abstract` base class instead, `-> void` overrides need no `return`.
228	
229	**Driver rules.** The driver iterates a fixed-size array, allocates nothing, checks `present.is_valid()` before each call and skips and counts a freed presenter (`PRESENTER_DEAD`, as ADR-0002 does for result handlers), and **never runs a presenter inside a tick**. Presenter faults cannot fault the kernel: nothing here runs in a tick phase. Stage timing exists in dev and playtest builds through ADR-0001's diagnostics timer and is compiled out of release.
230	
231	**The frame object is the clock.** `PresentFrame.alpha` is read once; no presenter reads `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` directly (a lint on `tick_alpha` outside the driver, the camera solver's pure-function twin and tests). This guarantees one alpha per frame. A presenter may read `frame.T` for values the simulation also computes (the beacon aim at `T`, a Graph step index); it **must never** use `T` or any tick counter as cosmetic phase (registry `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`), and uses `frame.present_time` for cosmetic phase.
232	
233	**Pause.** `PresentFrame.present_time` is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and `alpha` is 1.0, so a presenter that computes from `present_time` and `alpha` is frozen without being told. Layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table) keep running on engine time because they must respond while paused (PR-9); they are INPUT_SURFACE objects and UI Controls, not world presenters.
234	
235	### 4. Integer placement at `tick_alpha`
236	
237	One function, one owner, no other rounding anywhere in presentation.
238	
239	```gdscript
240	# src/presentation/placement.gd
241	class_name Placement extends RefCounted
242	## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
243	static func at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) -> Vector2i:
244		return Vector2i(floori(prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha), floori(prev.y + (curr.y - prev.y) * alpha))
245	
246	## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
247	static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
248		return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)
249	
250	## The only assignment point for a Node2D position in presentation. Skips an unchanged write.
251	static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
252		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
253		if node.position != v:
254			node.position = v
255	```
256	
257	**Rules:**
258	- Every moving thing in the current body frame is placed with `Placement.at` and written with `Placement.put`: sprites, the avatar, hand tools, the beam chest point, light origins, HUD plate anchors that follow world things, the single floored canvas offset of a non-avatar body (`Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, alpha)` with both offsets taken relative to the avatar's body, TR-shipbody-033), and the camera pose. The beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position, so light origin and sprite never disagree (PR-4 rule 2, TR-pc-026).
259	- **`floori`, never `int()`, `round`, `roundi` or truncation.** Probed 2026-10-28: `floori(-3 + 1 * 0.5)` is -3. Truncation and rounding both move negative-coordinate bodies by a pixel relative to positive ones.
260	- **Interpolate, then quantise (PR-4 rule 3).** Snap is a floor, not a filter: a body moving one base pixel per tick shows a k by k block step at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above, never backward. Nothing is rounded before the lerp.
261	- `alpha` is `frame.alpha`, in [0, 1], never extrapolated. `alpha_n` is legal only for a block whose owner publishes its run tick, is clamped at 1, and is floored by `at`. The sprite pose of a stepped rig (Horror) is not tweened; only the record's position is placed with `alpha_n` (PR-9).
262	- **Assignments to `position`, `global_position`, `transform`, `global_transform`, `offset` or `canvas_transform` on a `Node2D` or `CanvasItem` appear only in `placement.gd`** (and in the camera host's one `canvas_transform` write); a lint enforces it. A debug-build and integration-test sweep reads every `Node2D` under the world root once per frame in the scripted walk and asserts a zero fractional part (`PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` counts, test fails on non-zero).
263	- No per-node scale animation; horizontal flip is `flip_h` or a scale of -1 on x only; `Camera2D.zoom` stays (1, 1); rotation of human-built geometry is 0 (PR-4 rules 4 and 5). Cosmetic offsets (tremor of plus or minus 1 art px) are integers added after placement.
264	- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` are on as a safety net, set to their required values in `project.godot` by the Pipeline's guard rails (PR-15; probed: both default `false`). **Nothing in this ADR relies on them**; what they snap to under the SubViewport variants is ADR-0008's spike.
265	- An asset or one-off sprite uses even cell dimensions or `centered = false` with an integer `offset` (PR-4 rule 6); the asset lint is ADR-0010's.
266	
267	### 5. One interpolator: physics interpolation off, and no engine clock on sim-visible content
268	
269	**The pins.** `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false` in `project.godot`, written explicitly by the Pipeline's guard-rail block (PR-15; a value equal to the default is not serialised, so the tests read the effective value). The presentation root nodes set `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`; children inherit. `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false` and `limit_smoothed = false` where a `Camera2D` exists at all (the primary camera variant has none in the world tree, PR-6 C2).
270	
271	**The boot check, after the first frame** (probed: inheritance resolves in a running tree and not before): `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/common/physics_interpolation") == false`, `get_tree().physics_interpolation == false`, and a walk over every node under the presentation roots asserts `not node.is_physics_interpolated()`. A violation fails boot in dev and playtest builds and counts `PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_ON` plus logs in release. A gdUnit4 test additionally turns `SceneTree.physics_interpolation` on, builds the presentation tree, and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node, which proves the `OFF` roots rather than only the project setting.
272	
273	**Why not use the engine's 2D interpolation.** (a) It would be a second interpolator on a second clock (PR-4 rule 8). (b) Probed: `get_global_transform_interpolated` does not exist on `Node2D`, so no script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn, and the camera, which follows the un-interpolated pose, would swim against the sprite by 1 to 3 render pixels at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. (c) The kernel's previous and current pair is the only definition of the previous pose that survives a restore, a body transfer and a snap (`snap_baseline`, ADR-0003).
274	
275	**Engine clocks on sim-visible content.** `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D.play()` and `GPUParticles2D` at a non-zero `speed_scale` run on the engine's process time, which does not stop under kernel `PAUSED` (the tree is not paused, ADR-0001 § 6) and does not follow reduced motion. For world content (layer 0) and the HUD (layer 2) a presenter therefore **drives animation from `frame.present_time`** (a frame index computed from it, a shader time parameter set from it) or sets `speed_scale` to 0 while `present_time` is frozen. Engine-clocked animation is permitted only on layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table and menus), which must respond under pause, and on content that has no sim-visible meaning and is allowed to continue. Whether `speed_scale = 0` freezes a given node type exactly is UNVERIFIED (PRES-SPIKE-1).
276	
277	The bounded presentation-owned animation states are those PR-8 admits (camera state, and the instruments' `settle_response`), plus the cosmetic scalars of § 6.
278	
279	### 6. Presentation-local state, the restore edge, and pure-function presenters
280	
281	**What presentation may keep.** A presenter may hold a scalar or small structure (a needle's settle triple, a dwell counter, a tremor envelope, a fade, a cull history, the camera's smoothing state, a numeral throttle) **if and only if**:
282	1. it is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation (`src/kernel/` and `src/sim/` import nothing from `src/presentation/`);
283	2. it changes how a value *arrives* and never what it *settles to*, and never decides visibility of a truth-channel element (a trail's visibility depends only on the sim, which is why the Failure & Trail GDD calls it a pure reader);
284	3. it is reset by `on_discontinuity` on a restore, a new game, a camera cut and `hard_start` (TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047);
285	4. the presenter's registration lists it in a short doc comment so a reviewer can see the scalars (the lint cannot).
286	
287	**A presenter's drawn output is a pure function** of `(PresentationViews at this frame, PresentFrame, its resettable scalars)`. The first frame after a restore needs no special path: `ALL` rebuilds from views, `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` clears the scalars, and the kernel's `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so there is no interpolation across the break (TR-cmd-046, TR-horror-041, TR-attention-047, TR-webmap-039 restore half). A multi-beat stall plays at most one beat and never replays (TR-attention-047): a presenter keeps the last-seen sequence value it was shown, compares it with the view's, and on a jump of more than one shows the end state.
288	
289	**Edge detection by sequence counters.** A presenter detects a discrete source change by comparing a view's sequence counter to the value it last saw (`breath_src_change_seq`, TR-suit-041), not by counting notifications, because merged delivery turns N ticks into one batch. Because the notification, the dirty mark and the draw happen in one rendered frame, a click can start in the Audio stage and the dial swap land in the Instruments stage of the same frame.
290	
291	**The restore edge is not `ALL`.** `ALL` also means "more than 256 keys changed this frame" (a weld can do it), and resetting an instrument's tremor on a weld is wrong. The driver therefore watches a dedicated counter:
292	
293	```gdscript
294	# Requested of ADR-0001's PresentationClock (read-only, not a state block, never hashed or saved):
295	var load_seq: int:      # +1 on every transition into RUNNING that follows LOADING, and on every new game
296		get: return _driver_load_seq
297	```
298	
299	At the top of `frame(...)` the driver compares `clock.load_seq` with the last seen value and, on a change, calls every presenter's `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)` **before** any `present`. Camera cuts arrive the other way: the camera stage calls `driver.notify_camera_cut()` and the next frame delivers `DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT` (reset of instrument scalars and cull history; Instruments IW-33). `BODY_TRANSFER` is a rebase, not a cut, unless the new body's limits clamp (TR-shipbody-049, ADR-0008). If ADR-0001's owner declines the extra field, the equivalent is a composition-root-owned counter on the same clock object (ADR-0004's draft has no restore marker in `ChangeBatch`; its `is_all` on load is the same value as a mass change); the driver is the only consumer either way, so the choice does not leak into presenters.
